text_blocks.snippet: In Utah, [Highlight start] an asphalt shingle roof generally costs $4.50 to $12.00 per square foot installed (roughly $7,000 to $18,000 for a typical home), while a metal roof costs $12.00 to $20.00+ per square foot installed [Highlight end] (often $20,000 to $36,000+ depending on home size and metal type).
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] an asphalt shingle roof generally costs $4.50 to $12.00 per square foot installed (roughly $7,000 to $18,000 for a typical home), while a metal roof costs $12.00 to $20.00+ per square foot installed [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Asphalt 3-Tab Shingles: $4.50–$6.50 per sq. ft. installed; shortest lifespan (around 20 years).
Architectural / Dimensional Shingles: $6.00–$9.00 per sq. ft. installed; popular balance of price and durability (~30-year lifespan).
Class 4 Impact-Resistant Shingles: $8.00–$12.00 per sq. ft. installed; better for hail-prone areas and may qualify for insurance discounts.
Standing Seam Metal Roofing: $12.00–$20.00 per sq. ft. installed (metal shingles/tiles can also vary around $10–$16+ depending on profile).

text_blocks.snippet: Utah Factors That Affect Total Cost

list.snippet: Snow Load & Shedding: Heavy mountain and valley snow makes metal's smooth surface and 50+ year lifespan appealing in high-snow areas like Heber Valley, though snow guards or structural checks can add to the quote.
Hail & Wind: Impact-resistant shingles or durable metal panels hold up better against severe storms.
Labor & Installation Time: Metal requires more specialized labor and typically takes longer to install (often several days vs. 1–3 days for asphalt), increasing labor costs.
Roof Pitch & Complexity: Steeper pitches, dormers, valleys, and tear-off of existing layers raise material and labor totals.

text_blocks.snippet: If you share your approximate roof or home square footage, roof pitch/complexity, and whether you plan to stay long-term or sell soon, I can help narrow down the estimated cost range and best material option.
